correctness.rationale: The exact graph edge list and all shell sizes are recomputed. For all fifteen nonempty distance sets, the primary script enumerates faces, constructs distinct vertex-toggle matching pairs, and exhaustively topologically sorts every oriented Hasse incidence to establish acyclicity. Critical-cell counts prove all single-dimensional wedges and disconnected cases. For D={0,1,3} and {0,2,3}, independent integer signed gradient-path evaluation gives a zero 6-by-21 Morse attaching matrix, so Hurewicz proves the 3-cell attachments are null in the wedge of six 2-spheres. All counts and reduced mod-two ranks are independently reproduced by a second standard-library-only program. No experimental extrapolation or unproved infinite claim occurs.

value.rationale: This classifies every nonempty distance set of a canonical distance-regular polyhedral graph, rather than an arbitrarily selected instance. The construction and two initial ball cases are motivated explicitly in Previte (2014). The table identifies eight distinct homotopy types and completes that natural finite parameter landscape. The two omitted-middle-shell cases have a genuinely mixed integral wedge (six two-spheres and 21 three-spheres), which cannot be inferred from the earlier ball-case homology and resolves nontrivial attaching degrees. The precise benchmark is reusable in studying distance-indexed simplicial constructions, while no claim of a general theorem for arbitrary graphs is needed.
